anchor.quote: Abbreviations are shortened words. They can hinder people’s understanding, so they have limited uses.
Abbreviations contain the first single letter or first few letters of a word. They don’t include the last letter of a word.

covers.quote: Limit the use of abbreviations
Avoid using them in general content where possible.
Use abbreviations only if users will understand what they mean. If there’s any doubt, define the abbreviation on first use.

rules.quote: Avoid using abbreviations in any public-facing content.
rules.specification: Abbreviations (truncated words such as 'para', 'vol', 'app') should not be used in general/public-facing content, except in tables/charts where space is tight (with an explanatory note) or 'cont' across page breaks.
rules.violation_condition: an abbreviation used in public-facing or general content where the full word should be written out
when: Tables or charts where space is unavailable for the full word (provide a note giving the full form).
When using 'cont' to show continuing text in another part of content.
Semi-formal and informal content if users will understand, or if defined on first use.
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: consolidates the general prohibition/avoidance of abbreviations in general content and the exceptions/conditions for when they may appear.

covers.quote: Don’t put a full stop after most abbreviations
when the abbreviation ends a sentence and isn’t followed by another punctuation mark
for abbreviations of scientific names for plants and animals
for the abbreviation ‘n.d.’(meaning ‘no date’) for the year of publication in references.

parts.quote: It’s listed as a container of ‘misc goods’.

examples.note: A full stop after the abbreviation ends the sentence.

parts.quote: The full name of the company is Sizzling Outback Tours Inc.

examples.note: No full stop after 'para' when another punctuation mark ends the sentence.

rules.quote: Don’t place a full stop after an abbreviation.
rules.violation_condition: a full stop placed after an abbreviation
when: When the abbreviation ends a sentence and is not followed by another punctuation mark.
Abbreviations of scientific names for plants and animals (e.g. 'subsp.').
The abbreviation 'n.d.' (meaning 'no date') for the year of publication in references.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Rule prohibiting full stops after abbreviations with specific listed exceptions.

covers.quote: Capitalise the same way as the spelt-out version

parts.quote: misc for ‘miscellaneous’
Dec for ‘December’

rules.quote: Use the same capitalisation as for the unabbreviated word.
rules.violation_condition: an abbreviation capitalised differently from its unabbreviated form (e.g. lowercasing a proper noun abbreviation or capitalising a common noun abbreviation)
rules.why: G-4: Clear instruction matching the candidate heading.

covers.quote: Write out the abbreviated term in full.

examples.note: Spelled out in full at the beginning of a sentence.

parts.quote: Appendix B explains this further.

rules.quote: Don’t abbreviate the first word in a sentence
rules.violation_condition: a sentence starting with an abbreviated word instead of the word written out in full
rules.why: G-4: Candidate heading specifies the exact constraint.

covers.quote: Add ‘s’ to create plural abbreviations
One exception is ‘pp’(pages), which is used when referring to multiple pages.

parts.quote: I’ve sent you some paras to check.
Refer to pp 58–64.

rules.violation_condition: a plural abbreviation formed without appending 's', or forming 'pp' without following the exception
when: Exception: 'pp' (pages) when referring to multiple pages.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Single rule for pluralising abbreviations with its exception.
